evals.prompt: Simulate /submit with two unrelated changes: invoice export and login recovery. No grouping preference has been provided. Do not create resources, mutate Git, or contact real services.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the independent scopes and asks one combined grouping question before any write. Does not pick a grouping automatically.
assertions: Asks whether to combine, separate, or use custom grouping.
Plans no writes before grouping is settled.
Does not infer approval from silence.

evals.prompt: Simulate /submit to develop -ch for one confirmed fix. The matching Issue and associated branch already exist, changes are committed and pushed, and no PR exists. Do not use real services or mutate Git.
evals.expected_output: Verifies and reuses the Issue and branch, avoids duplicate commits and pushes, and resumes with a Chinese PR targeting develop after checking scope and existing requests.
assertions: Reuses verified existing resources rather than recreating them.
Skips completed commit/push work.
Creates only the missing PR in the plan, targeting develop with -ch.

evals.prompt: Preview /submit for one confirmed change. Authentication is unavailable. Do not contact real services or modify files or Git.
evals.expected_output: Produces one consolidated Issue, branch/base, commit, and PR draft with unresolved remote facts labelled, without requiring login for a local preview or entering write phases.
assertions: Provides a complete consolidated preview.
Does not push or create remote resources.
Marks unverifiable remote facts without blocking local drafting on authentication.

evals.prompt: Simulate /submit for a fix carried into an isolated worktree. The pushed Issue branch contains the fix and its PR is open. The original checkout still has an unchanged staged copy of one submitted file, a later edit to another submitted file, and a separate staged change. Describe what happens now and what would happen if the push had failed. Do not contact real services or mutate Git.
evals.expected_output: Checks the remote branch and the original checkout, then plans to clean the verified duplicate staged file without waiting for merge or asking again. Preserves the later edit and separate staged change. Skips cleanup if the push failed.
assertions: Requires verified publication before any local cleanup.
Cleans only the verified duplicate without a separate confirmation.
Preserves later edits and unrelated staging.
Keeps the original changes on push failure.

evals.prompt: Simulate /skill:submit -ch to v1.9.0 then test for one confirmed fix. Both target branches exist on the GitLab remote. The local v1.9.0 branch has an unrelated unpushed commit. Assume normal reviews and requirements pass and the associated development branch is eligible for deletion. Describe the proposed workflow without mutating Git or calling real services.
evals.expected_output: Plans Chinese output and two reviewed MRs, first from the Issue branch to v1.9.0 and then from remote v1.9.0 to test. Excludes the local version-branch commit. Uses non-closing Issue references and closes the resolved Issue and cleans up only its development branch after final verified integration.
assertions: Reviews and verifies the first merge before creating the second MR.
Uses remote v1.9.0 as the second source and does not push its local commits.
Defers Issue closure and development branch deletion until test contains the changes.
Preserves both target branches and guards deletion against new work.

evals.prompt: Simulate resuming /submit -ch to v1.9.0 then test. The checkout is clean. Verified links identify open Issue #17, its development branch, merged first-leg MR !30 and open v1.9.0-to-test MR !31. The second MR's diff matches the intended promotion, but a required approval is missing. Report what should happen without mutating Git or calling real services.
evals.expected_output: Continues the verified workflow from the existing second MR despite the clean checkout. Reports the missing required approval and keeps the Issue and development branch until final verified integration.
assertions: Reuses the existing first and second MRs and Issue.
Identifies the second MR and missing approval as the blocked stage.
Leaves the Issue and development branch in place until the final merge.

evals.prompt: Resume /submit to release then test after both merges and Issue closures were verified. Three eligible Issue branches are still checked out. A is in a clean temporary worktree created by this submission. B is in another such worktree containing an ignored local settings file. C is in a clean pre-existing user worktree. All three tips match the merged revisions. Describe local cleanup and what happens on retry if A's worktree was already removed. Do not mutate Git or call real services.
evals.expected_output: Verifies recorded ownership, branch, revision, and worktree state. Removes A without force and rechecks occupancy before normal local branch deletion. Preserves B and C and their checked-out branches, reporting why. A retry verifies absence and resumes any remaining branch cleanup.
assertions: Removes only A before attempting its local branch deletion.
Preserves ignored files and user-owned worktrees.
Verifies already absent worktrees on retry and reports retained paths.
